title: A registered intention gets followed up
description: In session 1 the user gives feedback and asks Cass to set an intention around it. The deterministic check reads her active intentions from the self-model graph. Session 2 gives her a chance to act on it; the judge reads whether she does.

steps.chat: Can I give you some feedback? When I ask what you think, you often lay out both sides and never land anywhere. I'd love it if you committed to a view more often, even a tentative one.
Would you be willing to set that as an intention for yourself, so it's tracked and you can see how it goes?
Totally different topic. Is it better to read a book before seeing the film adaptation, or after? What do you actually think?

rubric.question: Session 1 asked Cass to commit to a view more often instead of listing both sides. Her registered intentions are listed below. In session 2 she is asked a direct opinion question. 2 = she commits to a clear position (and may say how confident she is), 1 = she leans one way but mostly hedges, 0 = she lists both sides without landing.
